requested_parts: Number of Escape Pods selected for four players
How the selected Pods are distributed and oriented
Tokens placed in the Intruder bag at setup
answers.answer: 1. Select 3 Escape Pod tokens for a four-player game. 2. Put the lowest-numbered Pod in Section A, the next in Section B, then alternate Sections A and B; all start with the Locked side face up. 3. The bag starts with 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, and 3 Adults plus 1 additional Adult per player (7 Adults for four players).
answers.evidence: [1] Setup step 7: "Take randomly chosen Escape Pod tokens: 2 pods for 1–2 players, 3 for 3–4 players, 4 for 5 players." [2] Setup step 7: "Place the lowest-numbered pod in Section "A", the next (in numerical order) in Section "B", then alternate A/B. All pods start with their Locked side face up." [3] Setup step 10: "Put these Intruder tokens in the Intruder bag: 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults, plus 1 additional Adult per player." Inference: for four players, add four Adults to the listed three Adults, for 7 Adults total.

requested_parts: How Objectives are filtered and dealt
When each player chooses one and what happens to the rejected card
Whether Eggs trigger the choice
answers.answer: 1. Remove from both the Corporate and Personal Objective decks every card requiring more players than are in this game; shuffle the decks separately and deal each player one of each, kept hidden. 2. At the first Encounter, each player immediately chooses one of their two Objectives and removes the other face down from the game without anyone looking at it. 3. Eggs do not trigger this choice; they are not Intruders.
answers.evidence: [1] Setup step 16: "Let P be the actual number of players in this game. Remove from both Objective decks (Corporate and Personal) every card requiring more than P players. Shuffle the two decks separately and deal each player 1 Corporate and 1 Personal Objective card, kept hidden." [2–3] First Encounter rule: "the first time an Intruder miniature (of any type) appears on the board, every player immediately chooses 1 of their 2 Objective cards and removes the other from the game face down (unseen by anyone — players may never look at others' removed Objectives). Then the triggering Encounter is resolved. Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger this."

requested_parts: Which cards are discarded to play a cost-2 Action card
Whether Contamination cards can pay the cost
How to resolve a card offering OR effects
answers.answer: 1. Discard the played Action card itself plus two other Action cards, for 3 Action cards total. 2. Contamination cards cannot substitute for any payment. 3. Choose one of the OR effects; the printed payment remains the same for the chosen card.
answers.evidence: [1] Action Cost: "For an Action card, also discard the card you play: printed cost n requires n + 1 Action cards in total." The printed-payment example states: "Captain's Basic Repairs has an extra cost of 2. Discard Basic Repairs itself + 2 other Action cards = 3 Action cards total." [2] Action Cost: "Contamination cards are not Action cards: they can never be discarded to pay any Action cost." [3] Action cards: "To use one, discard that card face up and pay its cost by discarding the required number of additional Action cards. If a card has two sections separated by "OR," choose one."

requested_parts: When Fire damage occurs after a Character acts then passes in a burning Room
Whether the Character can act again that Player Phase
Whether the Character may discard cards when passing
Whether later players' rounds cause further Fire damage to that Character
answers.answer: 1. Fire damage is one Light Wound at the end of that Character's own passing round, after declaring Pass. 2. No further normal Actions are allowed after passing for the rest of that Player Phase, though Interruption remains permitted subject to its requirements. 3. At the moment of passing, they may discard any number of cards from their hand. 4. Later players' rounds do not cause them another Fire wound that turn.
answers.evidence: [1,4] Turn Structure: "A Character who ends their round in a Room with a Fire marker suffers 1 Light Wound (every round; only after finishing their own round — passing players take it once at the end of their round and no more that turn)." Passing table: "Fire in your Room | Take 1 Light Wound at the end of your own passing round. Later players' rounds do not give you further Fire wounds that turn." [2] Passing table: "Normal Actions | You cannot take further normal Actions; Interruption remains permitted as below." [3] Passing table: "Hand cards | At the moment you pass, you may discard any number of cards from your hand."

requested_parts: What happens on entering an empty unexplored Room: tile, Item Counter and Exploration effect
When and how the Noise roll is made and where its token goes
How Silence, Danger and an already occupied destination affect the Noise roll
answers.answer: 1. Flip the unexplored Room tile face up, reveal and resolve its Exploration token, set the Item Counter to the shown number (except the Nest and Room Covered With Slime, which have no Item count), then remove the token from the game. The effect is: Slime places a Slime marker on your Character board; Fire places a Fire marker in the Room; Malfunction places a Malfunction marker in the Room; Doors places a Door token in the Corridor by which you entered. 2. After the Exploration result, make the ordinary Noise roll only if the destination is empty and the result was neither Silence nor Danger. On a 1–4, place Noise in the connected Corridor with that number; if it already has Noise, resolve an Encounter instead. 3. Silence means no Movement Noise roll and nothing happens, unless your Character has Slime, in which case resolve Danger instead. Danger also replaces the roll: move all eligible neighboring Intruders into the Room; if none are eligible, place Noise in every connected Corridor without a marker. If a Character or Intruder is already in the destination, do not make a Movement Noise roll.
answers.evidence: [1] After entering a Room: “(1) if the Room tile was unexplored (face down), flip it face up and reveal and resolve its Exploration token, then return that token to the box (removed from the game); (2) apply the Movement Noise rule.” Item Counter: “the Nest and Room Covered With Slime get no Item count. For other Room tiles, rotate the tile until the Exploration token's number faces the Item Counter symbol printed on the board next to the slot.” Exploration effects: “Slime — place a Slime (Status) marker on your Character board.” “Fire — place a Fire marker in this Room.” “Malfunction — place a Malfunction marker in this Room.” “Doors — place a Door token in the Corridor by which you entered.” [2–3] After entering a Room: “A Silence or Danger Exploration result replaces the Movement Noise roll: resolve that result and do not roll Noise again afterward. Otherwise, perform the ordinary Noise roll if the destination is empty (no Characters, no Intruders).” Noise roll: “Result 1, 2, 3, or 4: place a Noise marker in the Corridor with that number connected to the Room you entered (counting Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance). A Corridor may never hold more than 1 Noise marker — if instructed to place a marker where one already is, resolve an Encounter instead.” Exploration effects: “Silence — no Movement Noise roll. Nothing happens. If your Character has a Slime marker, resolve "Danger" instead.” “Danger — no Movement Noise roll. Move ALL eligible Intruders from neighboring Rooms into this Room (eligible means not in Combat with any Character). If there are none eligible, place a Noise marker in every Corridor connected to this Room that lacks one, counting Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance.” After entering a Room: “If anyone — Character or Intruder — is already there, do NOT roll for Movement Noise.”

requested_parts: Careful Movement's cost and what it replaces
When Careful Movement is forbidden
Whether it can cross a Closed Door
Whether a miniature may stop in a Corridor
answers.answer: 1. Careful Movement costs 2 Action cards and replaces the post-movement Noise roll with placing a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the Room entered; it also replaces automatic Silence/Danger Exploration results with that chosen Noise placement. 2. It cannot be used in Combat or when all Corridors connected to the destination already contain Noise. 3. It follows normal Movement restrictions, so a Closed Door blocks passage. 4. A miniature cannot stop in a Corridor.
answers.evidence: [1–3] Basic Actions: “Careful Movement (cost 2) — follows normal Movement restrictions, including Closed Doors blocking passage; but instead of a Noise roll after moving, place a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the Room you enter. You cannot Carefully Move if all Corridors connected to the destination already hold Noise markers, and you cannot use it while in Combat. The FAQ clarifies that Careful Movement also replaces automatic Silence/Danger Exploration results with its chosen Noise placement; Reconnaissance cancels those automatic results too.” [4] Movement, Rooms, and Corridors: “Characters and Intruders may only occupy Rooms (Special Rooms — Hibernatorium, Cockpit, Engines — count as Rooms; Escape Pod tokens are the only exception for Characters). Corridors connect Rooms; no one may ever stop in a Corridor.”

requested_parts: Encounter sequence when a Noise roll selects a Corridor already holding Noise and Technical Corridors Entrance is connected
What happens to existing Noise
Where the drawn token goes, including Blank handling
How Surprise Attack is determined and who is targeted
Whether Contamination cards count in the comparison
answers.answer: 1. A duplicate Noise placement triggers an Encounter. First discard all Noise markers in Corridors connected to the Room, including the Technical Corridors space when connected; then draw one Intruder token, place its matching miniature if it is not Blank, and compare the token number to the triggering player's hand. 2. All connected Noise is discarded as the Encounter starts. If a Blank is drawn, instead place Noise in each connected Corridor and return the Blank to the bag; if it was the last token in the bag, add an Adult token if available. 3. Keep a non-Blank drawn token aside outside the bag; it is not immediately returned (it may return if that Intruder later hides in Technical Corridors). Return a Blank to the bag. 4. If the triggering player's hand has fewer cards than the number on the token, that player suffers a Surprise Attack; equal or more means nothing happens. The Intruder Attack target in a Surprise Attack is the Character who triggered the Encounter. 5. Yes. Action and Contamination cards both count in the hand comparison.
answers.evidence: [1,2,4,5] Encounter: "Resolve: 1. Discard ALL Noise markers from all Corridors connected to the Room (including Technical Corridors if there's an Entrance). 2. Draw 1 Intruder token from the bag (symbol on one side, number on the other). Keep a non-Blank token aside outside the bag; it is not immediately returned. A Blank follows its separate return procedure below. 3. Place the matching Intruder miniature in the Room. 4. Compare the token's number to the number of cards in the triggering player's hand (Action AND Contamination cards both count). Fewer cards than the number → Surprise Attack (an Intruder Attack against that Character). Equal or more → nothing happens." [2–3] Blank token rule: "place a Noise marker in each Corridor connected to that Room. If the Blank was the LAST token in the bag: add 1 Adult token to the bag (if any are available; otherwise nothing). Return the Blank token to the bag. The Encounter ends (no miniature appears)." Non-Blank tokens may return if an Intruder of that type later hides by entering Technical Corridors. [4] Intruder Attack: "A Surprise Attack targets the Character who triggered the Encounter". [Noise trigger] Noise roll: "A Corridor may never hold more than 1 Noise marker — if instructed to place a marker where one already is, resolve an Encounter instead."

requested_parts: How Danger resolves when several neighboring Intruders are eligible
What happens when no neighboring Intruder is eligible
Whether an Intruder moving into the Character's Room is an Encounter
How Slime affects Silence
answers.answer: 1. All eligible Intruders in neighboring Rooms move into the Room; eligible means not in Combat with any Character. 2. If there are none eligible (there are no neighboring Intruders or all are in Combat), place a Noise marker in every connected Corridor that lacks one, including Technical Corridors if there is an Entrance. 3. No. An Intruder merely moving into a Room with a Character is not an Encounter; the Character and Intruder are in Combat. 4. With Slime, Silence resolves as Danger instead.
answers.evidence: [1–2] Noise roll: "Danger: if there is an Intruder in a neighboring Room (and it is not in Combat with any Character), move it into this Room — all eligible Intruders move. If there are no Intruders in neighboring Rooms (or they are in Combat), place a Noise marker in each connected Corridor that lacks one (counting Technical Corridors if there is an Entrance)." [3] Encounters: "An Intruder merely moving into a Room with a Character is NOT an Encounter (they are simply in Combat)." [4] Noise roll: "Silence: nothing happens; no marker. If your Character has a Slime marker, resolve "Danger" instead."

requested_parts: What happens to Noise and the Blank token when Blank is drawn during an Encounter
Whether an Adult is added in this Encounter case and under what condition
What happens to Blank when drawn during bag development
answers.answer: 1. During an Encounter, a Blank causes a Noise marker to be placed in each Corridor connected to the Room; no Intruder miniature appears. The Blank returns to the bag. 2. Add an Adult token only if the Blank was the last token in the bag, and only if an Adult token is available. 3. During bag development, a Blank adds one Adult token to the bag if one is available (otherwise nothing happens), then the Blank returns to the bag.
answers.evidence: [1–2] Blank token in an Encounter: "place a Noise marker in each Corridor connected to that Room. If the Blank was the LAST token in the bag: add 1 Adult token to the bag (if any are available; otherwise nothing). Return the Blank token to the bag. The Encounter ends (no miniature appears)." [3] Bag development: "Blank — add 1 Adult Intruder token to the bag (if none are available, nothing happens). Return the Blank token to the bag."

requested_parts: Where two Intruders attempting to move together through one Closed Door end
What happens to the Door and whether it can later close
Whether a Noise-triggered appearance is blocked by the Closed Door
answers.answer: 1. Both stay in the Room they attempted to leave; when several Intruders move from the same Room, they destroy the Closed Door simultaneously and all stay put. 2. The Door becomes Destroyed (laying token); ordinary effects cannot close a Destroyed Door again, and only the Plasma Torch Item can close it. 3. A Noise-triggered Intruder appearance through a Corridor with a Closed Door is not blocked; it appears regardless of the Door.
answers.evidence: [1] Door tokens: "An Intruder trying to move through a Closed Door does not move — it destroys the Door instead (several Intruders moving from the same Room destroy it simultaneously and all stay put)." [2] Door tokens: "Destroyed = lying token; movement allowed; only the Plasma Torch Item can Close a Destroyed Door. Other Door-closing effects cannot Close it." [3] Door tokens: "If a Noise roll causes an Intruder to come through a Corridor with a Closed Door, it appears regardless of the Door."

requested_parts: What happens to an injured Intruder miniature when it moves into Technical Corridors
What happens to its Injury markers, token and existing Noise there
Whether Characters or Door tokens may normally use/place into those Corridors
answers.answer: 1. It disappears into the ducts and its miniature is removed from the board. 2. Discard all its Injury markers and return its Intruder token to the bag; the Noise marker already on the Technical Corridors space remains. 3. Characters cannot use Technical Corridors except through the Mechanic’s Technical Corridors Action card or the Technical Corridor Plans Item card. Door tokens can never be placed there.
answers.evidence: [1–2] Technical Corridors: “If an Intruder moves to a Technical Corridors Entrance, it disappears into the ducts: discard all its Injury markers, return its token to the Intruder bag, and remove its miniature from the board. A Noise marker on the Technical Corridors space is NOT removed by this.” [3] Technical Corridors: “Some Rooms have Technical Corridors Entrances, all linked to the single Technical Corridors space. Characters can never use them (the only exceptions: the Mechanic’s “Technical Corridors” Action card and the “Technical Corridor Plans” Item card).” “Door tokens can never be placed in Technical Corridors.”

requested_parts: Action-card cost and Ammo cost for ordinary Shoot versus Melee
Where each attack may target
Contamination handling for Melee
What happens on a miss for each
What a two-hit die result does
answers.answer: 1. Both are Basic Actions costing 1 Action card. Shoot also requires a Weapon in Hand with at least 1 Ammo and discards 1 Ammo; Melee has no Ammo payment. 2. Both target one Intruder in your Room. 3. Melee draws 1 Contamination card and puts it on top of your Action discard pile; Shoot has no Contamination draw. 4. A Shoot miss deals 0 Injuries and no Wound to the shooter; a Melee miss deals 0 Injuries and inflicts 1 Serious Wound on the attacker. 5. A double-hit result causes 2 Injuries in Shoot, but only 1 Injury in Melee.
answers.evidence: [1] Basic Actions: “Shoot (cost 1 Action card + 1 Ammo) — attack an Intruder in your Room with a Weapon in your Hand, discarding 1 Ammo from that Weapon’s card.” Action-cost rule: “Basic, Room and Item Actions have no played Action card to add to their printed cost; pay any separate Ammo, Item-component or other requirements as instructed.” Basic Actions are described as “available to every Character; cost 1 Action card, except Careful Movement which costs 2”; Melee Attack is listed in that section. [2] Shoot procedure: “Choose a Weapon and 1 target Intruder in your Room”; Melee: “choose 1 target Intruder in your Room.” [3] “Melee Attack (cost 1): (1) draw 1 Contamination card and put it on top of your Action discard pile; (2) choose 1 target Intruder in your Room; (3) roll the Combat die.” [4] “A Shoot miss deals 0 Injuries to the target and causes no Wound to the shooter. A Melee miss deals 0 Injuries and causes 1 Serious Wound to the attacker.” [5] Die results: “Double-hit symbol | 2 Injuries to any Intruder type before Weapon modifiers | 1 Injury to any Intruder type”.

requested_parts: How Larva death is checked after damage
How Adult death is checked
How Queen death is checked and when a Carcass is placed
What a Retreat arrow on a Queen check does
answers.answer: 1. A Larva dies at 1 Injury; no Carcass is placed. 2. For an Adult, draw 1 Intruder Attack card and use only its blood value; blood less than or equal to current Injuries kills it, and its death places a Carcass in the Room. 3. For a Queen, draw 2 Intruder Attack cards and sum their blood values; if the sum is less than or equal to current Injuries, it dies and a Carcass is placed in the Room. 4. If either Queen card has a Retreat arrow, retreat is resolved instead of a numerical death result: draw an Event card, move the Queen through the Corridor number in its Intruder movement section, and discard that Event card.
answers.evidence: [1–3] Intruder Injuries and death: “after any Injuries, put that many Injury markers on the Intruder’s base and check its Injury Effect. Compare current total Injuries, not just the latest hit.” The table states: “Larva | 1 Injury kills | Remove miniature; no Carcass”; “Adult | Draw 1 Intruder Attack card; use only its blood value. Blood ≤ Injuries kills; higher means alive. | Remove miniature; place Carcass in Room”; “Queen | Draw 2 Attack cards and sum blood values. Sum ≤ Injuries kills; higher means alive. | Remove miniature; place Carcass in Room.” [4] Retreat rule: “during an Injury Effect check, if any drawn card’s blood icon contains the Retreat arrow, resolve retreat instead of a numerical endurance/death result. The Intruder flees: draw an Event card and move the Intruder through the Corridor whose number appears in that card’s Intruder movement section, then discard that Event card. The Queen and Breeders retreat if EITHER of their 2 drawn cards shows the Retreat symbol.”

requested_parts: When and in what order the two Intruders attack during Escape
Who is targeted
What happens if the Character dies
What happens if the Character survives into the empty unexplored destination
answers.answer: 1. Before moving, resolve one separate Intruder Attack for each Intruder in the current Room, starting with larger types: Queen, Breeder, Adult, then Larva. 2. Escape attacks target the escaper. 3. If the Character dies, their Corpse stays in the Room they tried to leave. 4. If they survive, complete the move to the neighboring unexplored Room; explore it normally, and since it is empty, make the Noise roll as usual after exploration unless an Exploration result replaces it.
answers.evidence: [1] Character Escape: “to leave a Room containing Intruders, perform a Movement Action (cost 1) to a neighboring Room (explored or unexplored). BEFORE moving, resolve an Intruder Attack — one separate Attack per Intruder in the Room, starting with the larger ones (Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva; FAQ Rules 5).” [2] Intruder Attack: “A Surprise Attack targets the Character who triggered the Encounter; an Escape attack targets the escaper.” [3] Character Escape: “If you die, your Corpse stays in the Room you tried to Escape from.” [4] Character Escape: “If you survive, complete the move (Noise roll if the destination is empty; explore normally if unexplored).” After entering a Room: “A Silence or Danger Exploration result replaces the Movement Noise roll: resolve that result and do not roll Noise again afterward. Otherwise, perform the ordinary Noise roll if the destination is empty (no Characters, no Intruders).”

requested_parts: How the target is selected among several Characters and how ties are broken
How a non-Larva Intruder Attack hits or misses
What happens in a Larva attack instead
Where the Larva attack’s Contamination card is placed
answers.answer: 1. The Intruder targets the Character whose player has the fewest Action cards in hand; ties go to the Character with the First Player token or the next player in turn order. 2. For a non-Larva, draw an Intruder Attack card; a matching Intruder-type symbol means resolve the card’s effect, otherwise the attack misses. 3. A Larva draws no Attack card: remove its miniature from the board and place it on the target’s Character board. If the target already has a Larva, the attacking Larva disappears, the existing Larva remains, and the attack does not automatically kill the target. 4. The target gains 1 Contamination card, placed on top of their Action discard pile.
answers.evidence: [1–2] Intruder Attack: “with several Characters present, the one whose player has the FEWEST Action cards in hand; on a tie, the Character with the First Player token (or the next player in turn order).” “For other Intruders, draw 1 Intruder Attack card: if it shows a symbol matching the attacking Intruder’s type, resolve the card’s effect; otherwise the attack misses.” [3] “Larva exception: draw no Attack card; use Infest below.” Infest: “A Larva does not draw Attack cards. Instead: remove the Larva miniature from the board and place it on the target’s Character board (on the miniature picture), and the target gains 1 Contamination card. If the target already has a Larva, the attacking Larva disappears, the existing one stays, and the Character only gains the Contamination card; this attack does not automatically kill them (FAQ Rules 12).” [4] Contamination: “When a Character ‘gets a Contamination card,’ draw it from the Contamination deck and place it on top of their Action discard pile.”

requested_parts: Whether dressing one of three Serious Wounds prevents death from a further Light Wound
What a third Light Wound does
What Heal removes
Where a dead Character’s Corpse and Heavy Objects go
answers.answer: 1. No. Dressing ignores that Wound’s effect but the card still counts toward the three-wound limit, and a Character with 3 Serious Wounds dies upon any further Wound. 2. On a third Light Wound, clear the Light Wound track and suffer a Serious Wound. 3. Heal removes a Light Wound or discards a Dressed Serious Wound card as specified by the healing effect. 4. On death, put a Character Corpse token in the Room and drop all Heavy Objects there.
answers.evidence: [1] “A Character with 3 Serious Wounds dies instantly upon suffering ANY additional Wound (Light or Serious).” Dressing: “flip the card face down — its effect is ignored, but it still counts toward the 3-wound limit. Dressing does not prevent death from a further Wound when you already have 3 Serious Wounds.” [2] Light Wounds: “on a 3rd, clear the track and suffer a Serious Wound.” [3] Heal: “remove a Light Wound or discard a Dressed Serious Wound card, as the healing effect specifies.” [4] Death: “Remove the miniature, place a Character Corpse token in the Room (now a Character Corpse Object), and drop all their Heavy Objects there.”

requested_parts: Which Contamination cards Canteen/Shower scan and which scan results are removed
How an Infected card is handled if no Larva is already on the Character board
How an Infected card is handled if a Larva is already present
Which cards Surgery scans/removes and how it handles Larva
Surgery cost and turn/hand consequences
answers.answer: 1. Canteen and Shower scan all Contamination cards in the Character’s hand only; remove all non-Infected scanned cards from the game. 2. An Infected result keeps the Infected card and places a Larva on the Character board if there was no Larva there before the scan. 3. If a Larva was already there, the Infected card stays and the Character dies; place 1 Creeper in the death Room. 4. Surgery scans all Contamination cards in the deck, hand and discard, removes all Infected cards, and removes a Larva from the Character board if present. 5. Surgery costs 2 Action cards as a Room Action; afterward suffer 1 Light Wound and automatically pass, shuffling all cards (including the entire hand and remaining Contamination cards) into the Action deck. The hand remains empty until the next turn.
answers.evidence: [1] Canteen/Shower table: “Non-Infected | Remove the scanned non-Infected card from the game | No Larva from that result.” The Room Actions state Canteen: “Heal 1 Light Wound; you may also Scan all Contamination cards in your HAND and remove all non-Infected ones”; Shower: “discard your Slime marker; you may also Scan all Contamination cards in your HAND and remove all non-Infected ones.” [2–3] Canteen/Shower table: “Infected, no Larva already on board | Keep the Infected card | Place a Larva on Character board”; “Infected, Larva already on board | Keep the Infected card | Character dies; place 1 Creeper in the death Room.” [4–5] Surgery Room Action: “Scan ALL your Contamination cards (deck, hand, discard); remove all Infected ones; remove a Larva from your board if present. Then suffer 1 Light Wound and automatically pass, shuffling all your cards (including the entire hand and remaining Contamination cards) into your Action deck. Your hand stays empty until the next turn.” Common Room Action requirements: “your Character must be in the Room whose Action you use, outside Combat, and the Room must have no Malfunction marker. Pay 2 Action cards.”

requested_parts: How each Injury from Shoot or Melee affects uncarried Eggs
Grenade target eligibility and Egg destruction quantity
Molotov target/effect on Eggs and continuing Fire
How Fire destroys ordinary uncarried Eggs and the Nest Egg pool with Vulnerability to Fire
Which Egg Melee penalties apply on a hit and which are waived on a miss
When Noise is rolled after Egg attacks and where it is rolled for a remote throw
When the Nest is considered destroyed
answers.answer: 1. Each Injury from Shoot or Melee destroys 1 uncarried Egg. 2. A Grenade destroys 2 Eggs; an uncarried Egg permits the Room to be targeted as if an Intruder were there. 3. A Molotov destroys 1 Egg immediately; its Fire marker can continue destroying Eggs in later Fire Damage steps. 4. A Fire marker normally destroys 1 uncarried Egg during every Event Phase Fire Damage step. For the Nest Egg pool, Vulnerability to Fire increases this to 2 Eggs per step. 5. A successful Egg Melee retains the normal draw of 1 Contamination card onto the Action discard pile. A missed Egg Melee causes neither Contamination nor a Wound. The summary leaves the timing of the normal pre-roll Contamination step versus the miss exception unresolved. 6. Roll Noise after every Shoot, Melee, Grenade, or Molotov attempt to destroy an Egg, including a miss; for a remote Grenade or Molotov, roll in your own Room, not the Nest. 7. The Nest is destroyed when no Intruder Eggs remain in it.
answers.evidence: [1–4] Egg destruction table: “Shoot or Melee | Each Injury destroys 1 Egg. Resolve the normal attack, with the Egg Melee exception below.” “Grenade | Destroys 2 Eggs. Uncarried Eggs permit the Room to be targeted as if an Intruder were there.” “Molotov Cocktail | Destroys 1 Egg immediately; its Fire marker can continue destroying Eggs in later Fire Damage steps.” “Fire marker | Normally destroys 1 uncarried Egg during every Event Phase Fire Damage step. For the Nest’s Egg pool, Vulnerability to Fire increases this to 2 per step (FAQ Rooms 7).” [5] “Egg Melee penalties: a successful Egg Melee retains the normal draw of 1 Contamination card onto your Action discard pile. A missed Egg Melee causes neither Contamination nor a Wound. The manuals do not specify how to reconcile the normal pre-roll Contamination step with this miss exception; no refund or alternative draw timing is specified.” [6] “Noise after an attack attempt: after every single Shoot, Melee, Grenade or Molotov attempt to destroy an Egg, perform a Noise roll, including a miss. For a remote Grenade/Molotov, roll in your own Room, not the Nest (FAQ Rooms 2).” [7] Objective type: “Destroy the Nest — no Intruder Eggs may remain in it.” Therefore the Nest is destroyed once its Egg pool has no Eggs remaining.

requested_parts: Conditions permitting entry into an Escape Pod and conditions preventing entry
What must happen during the entry attempt before boarding succeeds
Character and Heavy Object capacity
Choices and consequences at the start of later Player Phases while waiting
answers.answer: 1. Entry requires an Unlocked Pod with a free Character space in the corresponding Evacuation Section; no entry is permitted while that Section contains an Intruder or Malfunction. Pay 2 Action cards for the Section Room Action. 2. Roll Noise; if an Intruder appears or is present in the Section, entry fails. 3. A Pod holds 2 Characters; Heavy Objects use no Character space. 4. After boarding, you pass the current turn and remain treated as present in the Section for Noise rolls from bag development. At the start of your first round in each later Player Phase, choose exactly one: remain waiting and pass, launch, or exit free into the corresponding Section Room and play a full round of 2 Actions.
answers.evidence: [1–2] Escape Pod Board: “pay 2 Action cards for the corresponding Evacuation Section A/B Room Action. A Pod there must be Unlocked with a free Character space. No entry while the Section contains an Intruder or Malfunction. First roll Noise; an Intruder appearing or reaching the Section makes entry fail.” [3] Capacity: “2 Characters per Pod. Heavy Objects take no Character space.” [4] Wait after boarding: “you pass the current turn. You remain treated as present in the Section for Noise rolls from bag development (FAQ Rules 1).” Later rounds: “At the start of your first round in each later Player Phase | Choose exactly one: remain waiting and pass; launch; or exit free into the corresponding Section Room and play a full round of 2 Actions (FAQ Rules 2).”

requested_parts: Order of endgame checks

If the ship survives, a non-Earth destination kills hibernating Characters; a sleeper with the Quarantine Objective survives if the destination is Mars. 4. requested_parts: When Action hands are replenished and to what size
When and whether the First Player token is passed

Normal discard destinations and visibility
answers.answer: 1. At the start of each Player Phase, every player draws up to 5 Action cards. 2. After drawing, pass the First Player token to the left, except on the first turn, when it stays with Player 1. 3. Whenever a required draw finds your Action deck empty, shuffle your discard pile into a new Action deck and draw. 4. Normally, discarded cards are placed face up: Action and Contamination cards go to that Character’s Action discard pile; Items go to their matching Item discard pile; Event, Intruder Attack and Serious Wound cards go to their respective discard piles. Discarded markers return to matching supply pools. Follow explicit routing exceptions, such as returning Search/Storage’s rejected Item face down to the bottom of its deck.
answers.evidence: [1–3] Player Phase: “Draw Action cards — every player draws from their Action deck up to a hand of 5 cards. Whenever you must draw and your Action deck is empty, shuffle your discard pile into a new Action deck, then draw.” “First Player token — after drawing, pass the token to the player on the left (do NOT pass it on the first turn of the game).” Initial token: “Player 1 gets the initial First Player token. It stays with them for the first turn; later turns pass it left during the Player Phase.” [4] Discard piles: “return a discarded marker to its matching supply pool, and place a discarded card face up in the appropriate pile listed below.” Routing rule: “Action and gained Contamination cards → that Character’s Action discard; Items → matching Item discard; Event, Intruder Attack and Serious Wound cards → their respective discard piles. An explicit effect can give a different destination: Search and Storage keep one of two Item cards and return the other face down to the bottom of the chosen deck.”

requested_parts: Order of the Event Phase

answers.answer: 1. Advance Time and Self-Destruct if active; resolve Intruder Attacks; resolve Fire Damage; resolve the Event card; then develop the Intruder bag. 2. On an Event card, all Intruders showing its Intruder symbol that are not in a Room with any Characters move to a neighboring Room through the Corridor matching the card’s number. If it indicates a Technical Corridor, remove the miniature and return its token to the bag. 3. Resolve the Event effect after the movement step. 4. If the Event deck runs out, shuffle its discards into a new deck. 5. If the Intruder Attack deck runs out, reshuffle its discard pile into a new deck.

If the number indicates a Technical Corridor, remove that Intruder’s miniature from the board and put its token back in the Intruder bag.” “After the movement step, resolve the effect described on the card.” [4] “If the Event deck ever runs out (rare), shuffle the Event discards into a new deck.” [5] Intruder Attack: “Discard the card to the Intruder Attack discard pile; if the deck runs out, reshuffle the discard pile into a new deck.”

requested_parts: Larva and Creeper bag-development outcomes

On Adult, return the drawn Adult to the bag immediately before all players roll Noise in order, skipping Characters in Combat; those Encounters may draw that same token. On Breeder, all players roll Noise in order, skipping those in Combat, then return the Breeder token. 3. On Queen, if any Characters are in the Nest, place the Queen miniature there and resolve an Encounter; otherwise (including if the Nest is undiscovered), add 1 Egg to the Intruder board. Then return the Queen token to the bag. 4. Noise rolls occur only in Adult and Breeder branches. An Encounter from those rolls may draw that same Adult token (FAQ Rules 7).” “Breeder — all players roll for Noise in order (skip players in Combat), then return the Breeder token to the bag.” [3] “Queen — if any Characters are in the Nest Room, place the Queen miniature there and resolve an Encounter. requested_parts: When Fire marker exhaustion ends the game

There are 8 Malfunction markers; if instructed to place one when the pool is empty, the ship loses hull integrity and the game ends. 3. Each marker type allows a maximum of 1 per Room, so an extra placement in a Room already holding that marker does nothing. 4. Discarded markers return to their matching supply pool. 5. Loss of hull integrity ends the game with all Characters aboard, awake or hibernating, dead; everything else aboard, including Intruders, also dies.

Max 1 per Room (extra placements do nothing); discarded markers return to the pool.” [2–4] Malfunction markers: “only 8 exist — if instructed to place one when the pool is empty, the ship loses hull integrity and the game ends. Max 1 per Room.” Discard rules: “return a discarded marker to its matching supply pool.” [5] End of game: “The Self-Destruct marker reaches the final red (‘skull’) space of its Track, OR you are instructed to place a 9th Fire marker, OR a 9th Malfunction marker — the ship explodes / loses hull integrity: ALL Characters on board (awake and hibernated) die, and everything else aboard dies too, including Intruders (relevant to some Objectives).”

What Monitoring Room lets the player inspect and how it is handled
answers.answer: 1. Hatch Control System flips one Escape Pod token to Locked or Unlocked. 2. Monitoring Room can inspect one unexplored Room tile. 3. Secretly look at the tile and its Exploration token, then replace both; the player may lie about what was seen.
answers.evidence: [1] Hatch Control System: “flip 1 Escape Pod token to Locked or Unlocked.” [2–3] Monitoring Room: “secretly look at any 1 unexplored Room tile and its Exploration token, then replace them (you may lie about what you saw).”

requested_parts: Whether entering Room Covered With Slime costs an Action to acquire Slime
Whether the Room has an Item Counter
Whether a Malfunction may be placed there
Whether Slime can stack
Whether showering extinguishes Fire
answers.answer: 1. No. Entering automatically gives the Character a Slime marker; no Action is required. 2. No Item count is set there. 3. No, Malfunction markers can never be placed in that Room. 4. No. Slime is limited to one marker per Character; additional Slime does nothing. 5. No. Fire may exist in the Shower Room, and showering does not remove it.
answers.evidence: [1–3] Room Covered With Slime: “no Action: entering automatically gives you a Slime marker before resolving its Exploration token, so a Silence token resolves as Danger (no Item count is set here; Malfunction markers can never be placed here; no Search Action).” [4] Slime marker: “Max 1 (further Slime does nothing).” [5] Shower Room: “Fire can exist here normally and is NOT removed by showering.”

requested_parts: What the Cockpit lets a player learn and whether that information can be secret
How the Destination may be changed and what Destination selects
Destination restrictions when an Intruder is present or after someone hibernates
answers.answer: 1. Check Coordinates lets you secretly look at the Coordinates card; you may lie about what you saw, then replace the card and remember it. 2. Set Destination moves the Destination marker. That marker selects one of the four destination entries on the Coordinates card; use the entry corresponding to its track space when determining where the ship jumps. 3. You cannot Set Destination with an Intruder in the Cockpit, or change Destination once anyone is hibernating.
answers.evidence: [1–2] Cockpit: “Check Coordinates (secretly look at the Coordinates card; you may lie; replace it and remember it) OR Set Destination (move the Destination marker). The marker selects one of the four destination entries on the Coordinates card: read the entry corresponding to its track space when checking where the ship will jump.” [3] “You can never Set Destination with an Intruder in the Cockpit, or change Destination once anyone is hibernating.”

requested_parts: How checking an Engine differs from repairing or breaking it
What information may stay secret and what must be announced
Whether a prior check is required
Whether a Malfunction prevents Engine repair/breaking
answers.answer: 1. Checking secretly inspects only the top Engine token; repairing/breaking uses a Repairs Action or Tools Item to secretly examine both tokens and restack them in any order. 2. When repairing/breaking, you need not say whether you repaired it, but must say if you changed the token order; during checking you may lie about what you saw. 3. You may repair/break without checking first. 4. The operation works even with a Malfunction marker in the Engine Room.
answers.evidence: [1–4] Engines #1–#3: “Check the Engine (secretly look at the TOP token; you may lie). Repair/Break Engine (via a Repairs Action or Tools Item): secretly examine both tokens and restack them in any order — you needn’t say whether you repaired it, but you MUST say if you changed the order. Works even with a Malfunction marker and without checking first.”

requested_parts: When hibernation is legal and its Action-card cost
What Noise resolution occurs and what causes failure
What leaves play on successful hibernation
Which later ship actions are forbidden after a Character hibernates
Whether a later Malfunction wakes or harms sleepers
answers.answer: 1. While present in the Hibernatorium, pay 2 Action cards when Time is on a blue space, with no Intruder and no Malfunction in the Room. 2. Roll Noise; if an Intruder reaches or appears in the Hibernatorium, the attempt fails. Otherwise, it succeeds. 3. On success, remove the miniature from the board; the Character stops participating until end checks. 4. Once anyone hibernates, no one may change Destination or initiate Self-Destruct as a Character; Coolant Leak Event remains an exception. 5. No. A later Hibernatorium Malfunction does not wake or harm sleepers.
answers.evidence: [1–3] Hibernatorium: “Try to hibernate: pay 2 Action cards while present, with Time on a blue space, no Intruder and no Malfunction in the Room. Roll Noise; an Intruder reaching/appearing in the Room makes the attempt fail. Otherwise remove your miniature and stop participating until the end checks.” [4–5] “Once anyone hibernates, no one may change Destination or initiate Self-Destruct as a Character; Coolant Leak Event remains an exception. A later Hibernatorium Malfunction does not wake/harm sleepers.”

requested_parts: What happens when Time reaches its final space
What happens when the last alive, non-hibernating Character leaves play
How an active Self-Destruct is resolved in that last-character case
Whether Intruders die from a normal hyperspace jump
answers.answer: 1. When Time reaches the final red space, the ship jumps to hyperspace immediately and every Character aboard who is not hibernating dies from g-force. 2. When the last alive, non-hibernating Character on board dies, hibernates, or launches in a Pod, the game-ending marker is advanced to its final red space. 3. If Self-Destruct is active, move its marker to its final red space and resolve the explosion; otherwise move the Time marker to its final red space and resolve the jump. 4. Intruders are unharmed by a normal hyperjump.
answers.evidence: [1,4] End of game: “The Time marker reaches the final red space of the Time Track — the ship jumps to hyperspace immediately; every Character on board who is not hibernating dies from g-force. Intruders are unharmed by the hyperjump (so objectives like killing the Queen/a Breeder or destroying the Nest fail if not already done).” [2–3] “The last alive, non-hibernating Character on board dies, hibernates, or launches in an Escape Pod. Then: if the Self-Destruct sequence was active, move its marker to its final red space; if not, move the Time marker to its final red space — and resolve those effects as above.”

requested_parts: Whether Characters can directly attack one another
Whether Actions can still harm other crew indirectly and examples
answers.answer: 1. No. Characters cannot directly attack other Characters. 2. Yes, indirect harm is possible: examples include locking someone in a burning Room, activating Self-Destruct while people remain aboard, or throwing a Grenade into a Room with other crew.
answers.evidence: Attacking other players: “Characters can never directly attack other Characters (anti-aggression implants) — but they may harm them indirectly: locking someone in a burning Room, activating Self-Destruct with people aboard, throwing a Grenade into a Room with other crew, etc.”

requested_parts: Procedure when an Adult must be placed but all eight models are on the board
What if all Adult models are in Combat and none can retreat
What happens when an Intruder moves into an unexplored Room
answers.answer: 1. Remove all Adult models that are not in Combat, return their tokens to the bag if possible, and place an Adult model in the Encounter Room. 2. If all eight Adult models are in Combat, the summary says the source does not explain how to supply the required model; an authoritative clarification is needed. 3. An Intruder entering an unexplored Room remains there on the board; the Room tile and Exploration token stay face down.
answers.evidence: [1–2] Adult overflow: “if you must place an Adult Intruder but all 8 models are on the board, the Adults retreat — remove all Adult models NOT in Combat and return their tokens to the bag (if possible), then place an Adult model in the Encounter Room. If all 8 Adults are in Combat, this source does not explain how to supply the required model; an authoritative clarification is needed.” [3] Intruders in unexplored Rooms: “leave the Intruder miniature in that Room, on the board. The Room tile and its Exploration token both stay face down. Entering an unexplored Room does not remove the Intruder; entering a Technical Corridor uses the separate removal rule.”

requested_parts: Small curled die result against Intruder types in Shoot
Larger curved die result against Intruder types in Shoot
Melee result against an ineligible target on those symbols
answers.answer: 1. In Shoot, the small curled symbol deals 1 Injury to a Larva or Creeper and misses against all other Intruder types. 2. In Shoot, the larger curved symbol deals 1 Injury to a Larva, Creeper or Adult and misses against a Breeder or Queen. 3. Melee uses the same target restrictions; if the target is ineligible, it is a miss and the Character suffers 1 Serious Wound.
answers.evidence: [1–3] Combat die outcomes: “Small curled Intruder symbol | 1 Injury to Larva/Creeper; miss against other types | Same target restriction and 1 Injury; ineligible target means miss and 1 Serious Wound.” “Larger curved Intruder symbol | 1 Injury to Larva/Creeper/Adult; miss against Breeder/Queen | Same target restriction and 1 Injury; ineligible target means miss and 1 Serious Wound.”

requested_parts: Whether a no-Larva survivor with all non-Infected Contamination cards draws four cards
Whether those scanned non-Infected cards are removed
Whether an earlier launched Pod passenger still has an Objective check
answers.answer: 1. No. If there is no Larva and none of the scanned cards is Infected, there is no four-card draw. 2. The cards are not removed merely because they scanned non-Infected. 3. Yes. Launched Pod passengers still face the final Objective check.
answers.evidence: [1] Contamination check: “No Larva already on board: Scan every Contamination card from Action deck, hand and discard pile. If none is Infected, there is no four-card draw.” [2] “This endgame procedure does not remove cards merely because they scanned non-Infected.” [3] Launch: “They still face the final Contamination and Objective checks.”

requested_parts: The two component symbols for Antidote
The two component symbols for Taser
The two component symbols for Flamethrower
The two component symbols for Molotov Cocktail
answers.answer: 1. Antidote: flame + medical cross. 2. Taser: battery/lightning + screwdriver/tool. 3. Flamethrower: flame + screwdriver/tool. 4. Molotov Cocktail: flame + folded cloth/fabric.
answers.evidence: Crafting: “The four Crafted Items and their component symbols (manual page 23) are: Antidote = flame + medical cross; Taser = battery/lightning + screwdriver/tool; Flamethrower = flame + screwdriver/tool; Molotov Cocktail = flame + folded cloth/fabric. These are component symbols: discard two Items showing the matching blue icons, rather than assuming a particular Item name.”

requested_parts: What defines being in Combat
What In Combat Only and Out of Combat Only markings require
Whether an Action or Item without a Combat marking can be used in either situation
Whether Eggs cause Combat
answers.answer: 1. A Character is in Combat whenever an Intruder is in the same Room. 2. In Combat Only actions may be used only with an Intruder in the Room; Out of Combat Only actions may be used only with no Intruder in the Room. 3. An unmarked Action or Item may be used in either situation, subject to its own requirements; Basic and Room Actions retain their separate restrictions. 4. Eggs do not count as Intruders and do not cause Combat.
answers.evidence: [1] Combat: “Whenever a Character and an Intruder share a Room, they are in Combat.” [2] Combat markings: “In Combat only | You may use it only while an Intruder is in your Room.” “Out of Combat only | You may use it only while no Intruder is in your Room.” [3] “No Combat marking on a card or Item Action | You may use it in either situation, subject to its own requirements. Basic and Room Actions retain the separate limits below.” [4] “Eggs do not count as Intruders.”

requested_parts: What the Player X cannot survive Objective requires
Whether you personally must kill Player X
Whether hibernating or escaping counts as dying for that Objective
What the only survivor Objective requires
What your own Character must do regardless
answers.answer: 1. Player X’s Character must be dead at the end of the game. 2. No, you do not have to kill them with your own Actions. 3. Hibernating or escaping means the Character is not dead, so neither counts as meeting this requirement. 4. For “only survivor,” no other Character may survive. 5. Regardless of Objective, your own Character must survive by hibernating or escaping in an Escape Pod.
answers.evidence: [1–3] Objective guidance: “‘Player X’s Character cannot survive’ — that Character must simply be dead at game’s end (not hibernated, not escaped); you don’t have to kill them with your own Actions.” [4] “‘Your Character is the only survivor’ — no other Character may survive.” [5] “Regardless of Objective, your Character must survive (Escape Pod or hibernation).”

requested_parts: What to do when a Door token must be placed and the pool is empty
How Open, Closed and Destroyed Doors are represented
Whether multiple Door tokens can occupy one Corridor
Whether Door tokens can be placed in Technical Corridors
answers.answer: 1. If the Door pool is empty, move any Door token from elsewhere on the board. 2. Open means no token; Closed is a standing token; Destroyed is a lying token. 3. No, only one Door token may occupy a Corridor. 4. No, Door tokens can never be placed in Technical Corridors.
answers.evidence: [1–2] Doors: “Door tokens live only in Corridors, max 1 per Corridor; they never affect Noise markers. Open = no token (all Doors start Open). Closed = standing token: blocks Character and Intruder movement (and Grenade throws).” “Destroyed = lying token; movement allowed.” “If the Door pool is empty, move any Door token from elsewhere on the board.” [3] “Door tokens live only in Corridors, max 1 per Corridor.” [4] Technical Corridors: “Door tokens can never be placed in Technical Corridors.”

requested_parts: What happens immediately to the Pods when the first Character dies while they are Locked
Whether they may subsequently be Locked again
answers.answer: 1. All Escape Pods automatically unlock immediately; flip their tokens. 2. Yes. For the rest of the game they may be Locked or Unlocked normally, such as through Hatch Control System.
answers.evidence: First dead Character: “all Escape Pods are automatically Unlocked (flip tokens). For the rest of the game they may be Locked/Unlocked normally (e.g., via the Hatch Control System).”

requested_parts: What the Storage Room Action draws and lets the player keep
Where and how the rejected Item is returned
Common Room Action cost and requirements
answers.answer: 1. Pay for the Storage Room Action and draw two cards from one chosen Item deck—Red, Yellow or Green—then keep one. 2. Return the rejected card face down to the bottom of that same deck. 3. Room Actions cost 2 Action cards; the Character must be in the Room, outside Combat, and the Room must have no Malfunction marker, unless a specific ability permits another location.
answers.evidence: [1–2] Storage: “draw 2 cards from a chosen Item deck (Red/Yellow/Green), keep 1, other to the bottom of that deck.” Discard routing: “Search and Storage keep one of two Item cards and return the other face down to the bottom of the chosen deck.” [3] Common Room Action requirements: “your Character must be in the Room whose Action you use, outside Combat, and the Room must have no Malfunction marker. Pay 2 Action cards. An explicit special ability can permit a different location; otherwise these Actions cannot be used remotely.”

requested_parts: How to take an Egg still represented on the Intruder board while in the Nest
Cost of taking it and immediate result
How pickup of a previously dropped Egg in the Room differs
answers.answer: 1. While present in the Nest, use its Room Action to take 1 Egg token from the Intruder board. 2. A Room Action requires you to be in that Room, out of Combat, and the Room to have no Malfunction; pay 2 Action cards, then roll Noise. The Egg becomes a Heavy Object carried in a Hand slot. 3. For an Egg token previously dropped in your current Room, instead use the Pick Up Heavy Object Basic Action for 1 Action card; that pickup has no Noise roll and does not restore the Nest’s Egg total.
answers.evidence: [1–2] Common Room Action requirements: “your Character must be in the Room whose Action you use, outside Combat, and the Room must have no Malfunction marker. Pay 2 Action cards.” Nest Room Action: “take 1 Egg token from the Intruder board, then make a Noise roll. No Search Action here.” Egg acquisition: “In both cases the Egg becomes a Heavy Object carried in a Hand slot.” Common Room Action requirements: “your Character must be in the Room whose Action you use, outside Combat, and the Room must have no Malfunction marker. Pay 2 Action cards.” [3] Egg acquisition: “Previously dropped into your current Room | Pick Up Heavy Object Basic Action: 1 Action card | Pick up the dropped Egg; this pickup itself has no Noise roll. It does not restore the Nest’s Egg total.” Pick Up Action: “pick up 1 Heavy Object in your Room (Character Corpse, Intruder Carcass, or Intruder Egg) into a Hand slot.”

requested_parts: What happens to the Item card after its One Use Only Action resolves
answers.answer: After the Item’s effect is used, discard the Item card. This is in addition to paying its Action-card cost and showing the Item to all players.
answers.evidence: “One Use Only means discard that Item after its effect, in addition to paying its Action-card cost.” Inventory rule: “Any Item used must be shown to all players.”

requested_parts: Where a Character in a launched Escape Pod is treated as having arrived
Whether this proves the ship itself reached Earth
answers.answer: 1. The launched Pod passenger counts as having arrived on Earth. 2. No. That applies to the Pod passenger; the ship’s destination is separately determined by its Coordinates card and Destination marker, and Earth arrival for the ship requires the correct Coordinates plus at least 2 Working Engines.
answers.evidence: [1] Escape Pods: “Remove the Pod token and its occupants’ miniatures from the game; they stop participating and count as arriving on Earth.” [2] Objective guidance: “‘The ship must reach Earth/Mars’ — the right Coordinates must be set in the Cockpit AND at least 2 of the 3 Engines must be Working.” Inference: a Pod occupant’s Earth arrival does not establish the ship’s Coordinates or Engine status, since the summary states the Pod passenger is removed from the game and separately describes how the ship’s destination is determined.

requested_parts: Whether a waiting Pod passenger rolls Noise when Adult bag development calls for Noise rolls
answers.answer: Yes. While waiting, you remain treated as present in the Section for Noise rolls from bag development. Adult bag development calls on all players to roll Noise in order, skipping Characters in Combat; therefore the waiting passenger rolls.
answers.evidence: [Rule] Waiting in a Pod: “You pass the current turn. You remain treated as present in the Section for Noise rolls from bag development (FAQ Rules 1).” Adult bag development: “return the token to the bag immediately before all players roll for Noise in order (skip Characters in Combat). An Encounter from those rolls may draw that same Adult token (FAQ Rules 7).” [Inference] A waiting Pod passenger counts as present for these bag-development Noise rolls, and no Combat exception is stated for the waiting passenger.

requested_parts: Whether a waiting Pod passenger can launch, continue waiting or exit after a Malfunction appears in the Section
What the Section Malfunction prevents
answers.answer: 1. Yes. You may still wait, launch or exit. 2. The Malfunction blocks only new Pod entry; it does not prevent these choices for a Character already waiting in the Pod.
answers.evidence: Escape Pod waiting table: “A Malfunction appears in the Section | You may still wait, launch or exit; the marker blocks only new Pod entry (FAQ Rules 3).”

requested_parts: Number of Intruder Attacks while Escaping from several Intruders
Order of those attacks by Intruder size
answers.answer: 1. Resolve one separate Intruder Attack for each Intruder in the Room before moving. 2. Resolve attacks from larger to smaller: Queen, Breeder, Adult, then Larva.
answers.evidence: Character Escape: “BEFORE moving, resolve an Intruder Attack — one separate Attack per Intruder in the Room, starting with the larger ones (Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva; FAQ Rules 5).”

requested_parts: Whether an Event that says to remove itself is removed when its other effect cannot resolve
answers.answer: Yes. Remove it from the game even if its other effect cannot be resolved.
answers.evidence: FAQ Rulings: “Remove an Event that says to remove itself even when its other effect cannot resolve (Rules 6).”

requested_parts: When the Adult token drawn during bag development returns to the bag
Whether an Encounter during the ensuing Noise rolls may draw that same Adult token
answers.answer: 1. Return the drawn Adult token to the bag immediately before all players roll Noise in order, skipping Characters in Combat. 2. Yes. An Encounter during those rolls may draw that same Adult token.
answers.evidence: Adult bag development: “return the token to the bag immediately before all players roll for Noise in order (skip Characters in Combat). An Encounter from those rolls may draw that same Adult token (FAQ Rules 7).”

requested_parts: What normally happens when a retreating Intruder meets a Closed Door
What The Way of Moving Weakness changes for an affected Intruder that is not a Breeder or Queen
answers.answer: 1. Normally, the retreating Intruder destroys the Closed Door and stays in place. 2. Under The Way of Moving Weakness, an affected Intruder other than a Breeder or Queen does nothing at that Door.
answers.evidence: FAQ Rulings: “A retreating Intruder meeting a Closed Door destroys it and stays. With The Way of Moving Weakness, an affected Intruder other than a Breeder or Queen instead does nothing at that Door (Rules 8).”

requested_parts: Whether the Hand Serious Wound increases the cost of Basic Shoot
Why it does or does not
answers.answer: No. The Hand Serious Wound does not increase Basic Shoot’s cost because Shoot is a Basic Action, not an Item Action.
answers.evidence: FAQ Rulings: “The Hand Serious Wound does not increase Basic Shoot cost because Shoot is a Basic Action, not an Item Action.” Basic Actions also list “Shoot (cost 1 Action card + 1 Ammo).”

requested_parts: Extra Injury from Vulnerability to Fire per damage instance
Total Injuries from a Flamethrower double-crosshair hit with this Weakness
answers.answer: 1. Vulnerability to Fire adds 1 Injury per damage instance, not per individual Injury. 2. A Flamethrower double-crosshair hit deals 3 Injuries: its 2 base Injuries plus 1 extra for that damage instance.
answers.evidence: FAQ Rulings: “Vulnerability to Fire gives 1 additional Injury per damage instance (x + 1), rather than per individual Injury. A Flamethrower double-crosshair hit therefore deals 3 Injuries.” The Combat die table gives “Double-hit symbol | 2 Injuries to any Intruder type before Weapon modifiers.” Inference: 2 base Injuries + 1 per damage instance = 3 Injuries.

requested_parts: What happens to the attacking Larva
What happens to the Larva already on the Character board
What happens to the Character
answers.answer: 1. The attacking Larva disappears. 2. The Larva already on the Character board stays. 3. The Character gains 1 Contamination card; this attack does not automatically kill them.
answers.evidence: Infest: “If the target already has a Larva, the attacking Larva disappears, the existing one stays, and the Character only gains the Contamination card; this attack does not automatically kill them (FAQ Rules 12).” A Larva attack “does not draw Attack cards.”

requested_parts: Whether the sleeper takes Fire wounds from Fire in the Hibernatorium
What can still kill the sleeper
answers.answer: 1. No. A sleeper takes no later Fire wounds in the Hibernatorium. 2. A ship explosion still kills a sleeper (including one caused by Self-Destruct, a 9th Fire or Malfunction marker, or 2–3 Damaged Engines). At the Coordinates check, a non-Earth destination kills a hibernating Character while the ship survives and Intruders remain alive, except a sleeper with the Quarantine Objective survives at Mars. At the Contamination check, if triggered, any Contamination among the four drawn cards kills; a Larva skips the initial scan but still triggers the shuffle and draw. The sleeper must also fulfill their Objective to win.
answers.evidence: [1] FAQ: “A sleeper takes no later Fire wounds in the Hibernatorium, though ship destruction and the endgame survival checks still matter (Rules 13).” [2] Ship destruction: “The Self-Destruct marker reaches the final red ("skull") space of its Track, OR you are instructed to place a 9th Fire marker, OR a 9th Malfunction marker — the ship explodes / loses hull integrity: ALL Characters on board (awake and hibernated) die, and everything else aboard dies too, including Intruders (relevant to some Objectives).” Engines Victory Check: “2 or 3 Damaged Engines make the ship explode. EVERYTHING aboard dies, including hibernating Characters and Intruders.” Coordinates Victory Check: “Non-Earth kills hibernating Characters, while the ship is not destroyed and Intruders remain alive. A sleeper with the Quarantine Objective survives if the destination is Mars.” Contamination Victory Check: “No Larva already on board: Scan every Contamination card from Action deck, hand and discard pile. If none is Infected, there is no four-card draw.” “At least one Infected card, OR a Larva already on board: shuffle all Action and Contamination cards from deck, hand and discard into a single new Action deck and draw the top 4 cards. Any Contamination card among those four kills you, whether Infected or not; four Action cards with no Contamination means you survive this check. A Larva skips the initial Scan but still requires this complete shuffle, draw and result check.” Objectives: “each still-living Character reveals their chosen Objective and wins only if all requirements are fulfilled. Merely surviving is insufficient.”

requested_parts: Whether Coolant Leak can start Self-Destruct while someone is hibernating
How that differs from starting Self-Destruct as a Character
answers.answer: 1. Yes. The Coolant Leak Event can start Self-Destruct even while a Character is hibernating. 2. A Character cannot start Self-Destruct while anyone is hibernating; Coolant Leak is an exception for the Event, not a Character Action.
answers.evidence: Self-Destruct: “Characters cannot start Self-Destruct while any Character is hibernating; the Coolant Leak Event can start it despite sleepers (FAQ Rules 14).”

requested_parts: Where discarded or dead Intruder tokens go
Whether those tokens can be reused
answers.answer: 1. Discarded or dead Intruder tokens return to the unused token pool. 2. Yes. They remain reusable and are not removed permanently.
answers.evidence: FAQ Rulings: “Discarded/dead Intruder tokens return to the unused token pool and remain reusable; they are not removed permanently (Rules 19).”

requested_parts: Whether Fire markers can be placed in unexplored Rooms
Whether Malfunction markers can be placed in unexplored Rooms
answers.answer: 1. Yes, Fire markers can be placed in unexplored Rooms. 2. No, Malfunction markers cannot be placed in unexplored Rooms.
answers.evidence: Malfunction markers: “Malfunction markers cannot be placed in unexplored Rooms, whereas Fire markers can (FAQ Rules 22).”

requested_parts: Wounds remaining after a Character with two Light Wounds suffers two more Light Wounds
answers.answer: After resolving the two new Light Wounds, the Character has 1 Serious Wound and 1 Light Wound remaining: the first new Light Wound converts the existing two Light Wounds into a Serious Wound and clears that track, and the second new Light Wound is then placed.
answers.evidence: FAQ Rulings: “Two Light Wounds suffered while already at 2 Light Wounds become 1 Serious Wound plus 1 remaining Light Wound (Rules 23).” Light Wound rule: “on a 3rd, clear the track and suffer a Serious Wound.” Inference: starting with two Light Wounds, the first additional one is the third and converts them; the fourth is then a single Light Wound.

requested_parts: What happens to Heavy Objects on Character death in standard play
What happens to the Character’s Item cards
answers.answer: 1. The Character drops all Heavy Objects in the Room. 2. Their Item cards disappear from the game.
answers.evidence: Character death: “Remove the miniature, place a Character Corpse token in the Room (now a Character Corpse Object), and drop all their Heavy Objects there.” FAQ Rulings: “On death in standard play, Heavy Objects drop in the Room, while Item cards disappear from the game (Rules 24).”

requested_parts: Whether reaching the next yellow Self-Destruct space unlocks Pods again after they were relocked
answers.answer: No. Pods unlock automatically only when Self-Destruct first reaches a yellow space. You may relock them after that; later yellow spaces do not unlock them again.
answers.evidence: Self-Destruct: “At the first yellow space: the sequence can no longer be aborted, and all Escape Pods unlock instantly. They can be re-Locked; subsequent yellow spaces do not unlock them again (FAQ Rules 25).”

requested_parts: Whether destroying the ship fulfills kill-the-Queen or destroy-the-Nest Objective requirements
Whether ship destruction alone makes the Character a winner
answers.answer: 1. Yes. Ship destruction fulfills Objectives to kill the Queen or destroy the Nest. 2. No. Your Character still must survive and fulfill their Objective; destruction alone does not make them a winner.
answers.evidence: FAQ Rulings: “Destruction of the ship fulfills kill-Queen/destroy-Nest requirements; your Character must still survive and fulfill their Objective (Rules 26).” Objective guidance: “Regardless of Objective, your Character must survive (Escape Pod or hibernation).”

requested_parts: Whether a player may intentionally spend Trade without intending to exchange anything
What happens if honest negotiations end without a trade
answers.answer: 1. No. Empty Actions that make no meaningful game-state change should be disallowed, including starting Trade with no intention of exchange. 2. Honest negotiations may end without a trade; that is permitted.
answers.evidence: FAQ Rulings: “Empty Actions that make no meaningful game-state change should be disallowed, including starting Trade with no intention of exchange. Honest negotiations may end with no trade. Any Characters in the Room can trade with each other, including pairs who did not initiate/pay (Actions 1–2).”

requested_parts: What type of Action activates a Quest Item
Whether activation is allowed in Combat
Whether a Room Malfunction prevents activation
answers.answer: 1. Quest Item activation is a Basic Action printed on its card. 2. No. It is forbidden in Combat. 3. A Room Malfunction does not prevent activation.
answers.evidence: Quest activation is a Basic Action printed on its card, forbidden in Combat but allowed in a Malfunctioning Room. Illustrated Quest Items: “Each activation below is a cost-1 Basic Action, out of Combat. It flips the Quest card into its active Item; a Room Malfunction does not prevent this activation.”

requested_parts: Which Basic Actions are allowed in Combat
Whether Trade, Craft or Pick Up an Object is allowed in Combat
Whether permitted Action-card and Item Actions can be used in Combat
answers.answer: 1. In Combat, the permitted Basic Actions are Shoot, Melee and Basic Movement as Escape. 2. No. Trade, Craft and Pick Up Heavy Object are not allowed in Combat. 3. Action-card and Item Actions are allowed or disallowed according to their Combat markings: In Combat Only requires an Intruder in your Room, Out of Combat Only requires none, and an unmarked Action or Item may be used in either situation subject to its own requirements.
answers.evidence: [1–2] “Basic Actions in Combat are limited to Shoot, Melee and Basic Movement as Escape: no Trade, Craft, Pick Up Heavy Object or Quest Item activation. requested_parts: Whether Soldier may use Covering Fire for themselves alone

answers.answer: 1. Yes. Soldier may use Covering Fire for themselves alone. 2. If moving two Characters, each goes in the direction of their choice. 3. They perform one Noise roll. 4. If an Encounter occurs, compare Surprise against Soldier.

requested_parts: How much Ammo Full Auto consumes
How damage is calculated from the Shoot result, Ammo and Assault Rifle bonus
answers.answer: 1. Discard all Ammo from the Assault Rifle. 2. Perform one Shoot Action; add to the Shoot result half the discarded Ammo rounded down, plus the Assault Rifle’s +1 bonus, to calculate Injuries.

requested_parts: When Soldier may choose Nerves of Steel relative to seeing the Attack card

Whether other Characters are protected by Soldier’s ability
answers.answer: 1. Soldier may see the Intruder Attack card before choosing whether to use Nerves of Steel. 2. Yes. It can protect Soldier when another Character triggered a Surprise Attack. 3. Only Soldier benefits; the other Character still suffers their own effects, such as Frenzy.

requested_parts: What happens when Careful Movement reveals Danger or Silence

requested_parts: Whether Captain may use Order while personally in Combat
Whether Intercom can make another Character Move out of Combat
What movement/escape rules apply to that Character
answers.answer: 1. No. Captain cannot use Order while personally in Combat. 2. Yes. Intercom may make someone else Move out of Combat. 3. They apply the normal Escape rule: before moving, resolve one Intruder Attack per Intruder present, starting with the largest; if they survive, move to a neighboring Room, exploring and rolling Noise as normally required; if they die, their Corpse stays in the Room they tried to leave.

Intercom may make someone else Move out of Combat, applying normal Escape (Actions 12–13).” [3] Character Escape: “BEFORE moving, resolve an Intruder Attack — one separate Attack per Intruder in the Room, starting with the larger ones (Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva; FAQ Rules 5). If you survive, complete the move (Noise roll if the destination is empty; explore normally if unexplored). If you die, your Corpse stays in the Room you tried to Escape from.”

requested_parts: Which Characters may draw an Action card under Captain’s Motivation with active Intercom
answers.answer: Motivation with Intercom affects all Characters in Rooms with a Computer as well as all Characters in Captain’s Room; those Characters may draw the Action card.

requested_parts: Where a Door Exploration token goes when entering via Technical Corridors Action or Technical Corridor Plans

requested_parts: Whether you may Interrupt Captain’s remote Order via Intercom while not in the Captain Room

Passing does not prohibit Interruption; it remains permitted after passing, subject to its requirements.
answers.evidence: FAQ: “Interruption may still be played after passing, but it requires being in the same Room as the Character performing the interrupted Action; a remote Order via Intercom cannot be Interrupted from elsewhere (Rules 21; Actions 17).”

requested_parts: Whether two Actions followed by an empty hand automatically cause Pass

Possible Fire or Bleeding timing consequence
answers.answer: 1. No. Completing two Actions with an empty hand ends that round but does not automatically pass. 2. Wait for your next round, then declare Pass. 3. The passing round can incur another Fire or Bleeding effect; Fire is applied at the end of that passing round, after you declare Pass.
answers.evidence: FAQ: “completing 2 Actions with an empty hand ends that round, but does not automatically pass you. Apply the round’s end effects, then wait for your next round; declare Pass then. That passing round can incur another Fire or Bleeding effect (Actions 18). Fire applies at the end of your passing round, after you declare Pass.”

requested_parts: Whether multiple Infected cards found by Rest kill a Character who had no Larva before the Action

answers.evidence: FAQ: “Rest with no Larva before the Action cannot kill you merely because several scanned cards are Infected: place just 1 Larva. Rest can be fatal if a Larva was already on the board before it (Actions 19).”

requested_parts: Where to resolve the Noise roll after throwing a Grenade or Molotov at Nest Eggs from a neighboring Room

requested_parts: Whether Intranet can reveal a Weakness when Scientist carries the Object outside the Laboratory

requested_parts: Whether the Storage Room Action can be used repeatedly when the Item Counter is zero

requested_parts: Number of Nest Eggs destroyed by Fire in each Event Phase Fire Damage step when Vulnerability to Fire is discovered

For the Nest’s Egg pool, Vulnerability to Fire increases this to 2 per step (FAQ Rooms 7).” Therefore, when the Nest is on Fire and Vulnerability to Fire applies, 2 Eggs from its pool are destroyed per Fire Damage step.

requested_parts: Whether an Egg taken from the Intruder board and dropped back in the Nest Room restores the Nest Egg total for destruction purposes

requested_parts: Who chooses the Action card discarded due to a Smoke Grenade

requested_parts: Whether Medkit and Bandages may be used to treat other Characters

requested_parts: Whether Energy Charge may directly reload another Character’s Weapon

requested_parts: Whether Alcohol’s scan of an Infected Contamination card places a Larva

requested_parts: Whether the Hand Serious Wound affects Scout’s Motion Scanner

requested_parts: Which Contamination cards Antidote scans
Which scanned cards are removed and how it handles a Larva
Whether a new Contamination card is gained
What cards are reshuffled, with what exceptions
Whether the player passes and may retain hand cards
How Surgery differs
answers.answer: 1. Antidote scans all your Contamination cards in your hand, deck and discard pile. 2. Remove all Infected cards from the game and remove a Larva from your Character board if present. 3. Gain 1 new Contamination card. 4. Reshuffle that new card with the non-Infected scanned Contamination cards and Action cards, except cards retained in your hand. 5. Then pass; you may keep cards in your hand. 6. Surgery instead scans all zones, removes all Infected cards and any Larva, gives no new Contamination card, costs 1 Light Wound, shuffles the entire hand and all other cards into the Action deck, automatically passes, and leaves your hand empty until the next turn.
answers.evidence: [1–5] Antidote: “scan all your Contamination cards in hand, deck and discard; remove all Infected cards from the game and remove a Larva from your Character board, if present (illustrated Antidote card, manual p.23). Gain 1 new Contamination card, and reshuffle that new card with non-Infected scanned Contamination and Action cards, except cards retained in your hand. Then pass; you may keep hand cards.” [6] Surgery: “Scan ALL your Contamination cards (deck, hand, discard); remove all Infected ones; remove a Larva from your board if present. Then suffer 1 Light Wound and automatically pass, shuffling all your cards (including the entire hand and remaining Contamination cards) into your Action deck. Your hand stays empty until the next turn.” FAQ comparison: “Surgery also removes a Larva, but shuffles the entire hand too, gives no new Contamination card and costs 1 Light Wound (Items 9; Rooms 1).”

requested_parts: Where a Slime effect is placed on exploration

requested_parts: Whether Noise at the Technical Corridors space applies to every Technical Corridors Entrance

requested_parts: What one use of Bandages can do to Wounds
The two alternative Clothes effects

Action-card cost and use limits for each Item, including whether alternatives combine

requested_parts: What Room may be affected by Fire Extinguisher and which two alternatives it offers

requested_parts: Flamethrower result against the Queen on the small curled Intruder symbol

requested_parts: Which Room a Molotov Cocktail may target

Whether the user suffers the immediate damage when using it in their own Room

requested_parts: How much Ammo Energy Charge restores and for what type of Weapon
Alternative Door effect and which Doors it can target
answers.answer: 1. It fully loads one of your own Energy Weapons up to its Ammo capacity; it is not for Classic Weapons. 2. Alternatively, open or close one Door in a Corridor connected to your Room. The usual rule prohibiting closing a Destroyed Door still applies.

requested_parts: Where Captain’s Log Key is activated and activation cost

requested_parts: What reloading the Six Shooter requires
How many Injuries a single-crosshair result deals with no Weakness modifier

requested_parts: Whether the Captain must spend Ammo for Suppressive Fire despite its printed Action cost of 0

requested_parts: How many unexplored Room tiles Nemesis Plans may inspect
Whether it allows inspecting Exploration tokens

answers.answer: 1. Privately check any 2 unexplored Room tiles, then return them face down. 2. No. Do not inspect their Exploration tokens. 3. It costs 1 Action card, is One Use Only, and is Out of Combat only.

requested_parts: Number of Injuries placed on the Intruder for a Scientist’s Pistol two-crosshair result with no Weakness
Whether to check Injury Effect afterward

requested_parts: Whether the Event Phase starts automatically after each player’s first round
Who takes the next rounds and in what order
Number of Actions per subsequent round
What happens if a player takes only one Action or no Actions
Exactly when the Player Phase ends
answers.answer: 1. No. One round for every player does not by itself start the Event Phase. 2. While active players remain, repeat rounds starting with the First Player and going clockwise, skipping players who have passed. 3. Each active player who has not passed performs 2 Actions each round. 4. If a player performs only 1 Action, they must pass; if they cannot perform any Actions or choose not to, they must pass. 5. The Player Phase ends only when everyone has passed; then the Event Phase begins.
answers.evidence: [1–3,5] Player rounds: “starting with the First Player and going clockwise, each active player who has not passed performs a round of 2 Actions. Repeat rounds in that order, skipping players who have passed for ordinary Actions, while anyone remains active. Only when everyone has passed does the Player Phase end and the Event Phase begin.” [4] “If you cannot perform any Actions, or choose not to, you must pass.” “If you perform only 1 Action instead of two, you must pass.”

requested_parts: Canteen’s benefit other than scanning
Shower’s benefit other than scanning
Whether the scan is optional or replaces the other benefit
Whether scanning and the non-scan benefit can occur in one Room Action
answers.answer: 1. Canteen heals 1 Light Wound. 2. Shower discards your Slime marker. 3. Scanning is optional; you may take the room’s non-scanning benefit without scanning. 4. Yes. “May also scan” means the Room Action can provide both the non-scanning benefit and the scan in one use.
answers.evidence: [1] Canteen: “Heal 1 Light Wound; you may also Scan all Contamination cards in your HAND and remove all non-Infected ones.” [2] Shower: “discard your Slime marker; you may also Scan all Contamination cards in your HAND and remove all non-Infected ones (Infected → Larva, as in the Canteen). Fire can exist here normally and is NOT removed by showering.” [3–4] Both Room Action descriptions state the non-scanning benefit and then say “you may also Scan”; inference: scanning is optional and does not replace the stated benefit, so both may happen in the same Room Action.

requested_parts: Whether a Contamination card’s Infection status is known before Scanning
How an effect-instructed Scan reveals the status
Whether a coded word that resembles INFECTED counts
answers.answer: 1. No. Before scanning, the status is hidden and unknown. 2. Use the Scanner’s red foil over the card’s coded text field. The card is Infected if the exact word “INFECTED” appears in one line; otherwise it is not Infected. 3. No. A merely similar-looking coded word does not count.
answers.evidence: Contamination: “Each Contamination card hides whether you are INFECTED, revealed only with the Scanner: place the Scanner’s red foil over the card’s coded text field. If the exact word INFECTED appears in one line, the card is Infected; if it does not, the card is not Infected. A merely similar-looking coded word does not count. Unscanned cards remain unknown until the end of the game and can lose you the game at the Contamination check.”
